To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the North Shore region is vulnerable to sea level rise and storm surge; 2) the most vulnerable areas are the surf tourism areas and developed areas; and 3) the most appropriate strategies to reduce vulnerability are beach nourishment and vegetative cover in developed and surf tourism areas; and artificial reefs in bentic habitat dominated areas.

in a high wave energy environment, the most appropriate adaptation strategies include expansion or construction of artificial reefs in areas with high wave exposure and benthic habitats, vegetative cover and/or beach nourishment in surf tourism and developed areas, and shoreline hardening in areas with high human exposure.
the best adaptation strategies for high-energy waves are artificial reefs, beach nourishment, and dune restoration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated approach for assessing vulnerability and identifying adaptation strategies for coastal communities threatened by sea level rise and high wave energy.
the application of a generalized framework to a high-energy wave environment and the identification of the most effective adaptation strategies.
developing a framework for assessing vulnerability to sea level rise, accounting for the unique characteristics and impacts in high energy wave areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the North Shore of Oahu, Hawaii is a high energy wave environment and the most viable adaptation strategies are expansion of artificial reefs and beach nourishment.
the most appropriate adaptation strategies in high energy wave environment are artificial reefs in the benthic habitat, beach nourishment, and vegetative cover in developed and surf tourism areas.

this study provides a methodological approach to assessing coastal vulnerability in high-energy wave environment and provides a framework for identifying and prioritizing adaptation strategies to sea level rise and storm events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of hard and soft measures are needed to protect the North Shore region from the impacts of sea-level rise.
the most vulnerable areas to sea level rise are those that have the most developed infrastructure.
a combination of beach nourishment, artificial reefs, and dune construction is the most cost-effective adaptation strategy for this area.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of strategies, including artificial reefs, beach nourishment, dune stabilization, and elevation or relocations are most likely to be effective and cost-effective in high energy environments.
a comprehensive assessment of the coastal environment, including the biophysical and socioeconomic factors, is essential to develop effective adaptation measures.
adaptation strategies must be customized based on the biophysical setting and the community's needs.
